title: PHP2Shell Exploitation on Check Point Gateway
content_md: Key findings Beginning on 30 October 2026, an attacker executed scanning and exploitation activity against organizations with unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, using Mobile Access portals with PHP2Shell as initial access followed by CVE-2026-123039. The first wave, on October 30, targeted Israeli organizations and included destructive activity against some of them. A broader second wave on November 2 targeted organizations across multiple countries and sectors, with no evidence of destructive activity In the investigated intrusion, PHP2Shell provided initial access, followed by privilege escalation through the DynamicCLI interface, tracked as CVE-2026-123039. The attackers then deployed PHP webshells, the persistent TSGA backdoor and its embedded TSProxy networking component. The attackers pivoted from the gateway to a VMware ESXi host over SSH, deployed the destroy_v6 wiper, and left politically themed DREAM_ANNEXATION.txt notes during the destructive stage. TSGA and TSProxy are modified variants of PhiliKit, a malware framework previously documented in attacks exploiting Ivanti vulnerabilities. Both tools share distinctive code, configuration, and cryptographic material with the framework Alth
